Stay out of Excel Hell

​

Microsoft recently added a Navigation Pane to Excel. The new navigation pane makes it much easier to explore the different sheets and sections in a workbook. You can think of the Navigation Pane as an electronic Table of Contents. Below is a video explaining this new feature, a worksheet from the video, and a brief explanation of the new functionality.

​

​

Download the Practice Worksheet

​

One can access the Navigation Pane by going to the view menu and clicking on the Navigation button.

​

Once you click on the Navigation button view, you will see Figure 2 on the right-hand side. The Navigation Pane will include a search section where you can look for sheets and objects within your workbook. Each worksheet will be listed with an arrow to expand the worksheet and see details about what is on the worksheet.

​

​

When you click on the Cover Sheet in the Navigation pane, you will see a list of objects on the page. The first is the image of the Arrow in A1, and you will see it gives a name to the object. Next is the one called Picture 2, which is the logo of The FP&A Guy. Below that, you see grids along with the range of text, for example, 'CoverSheet'!A15 is showing that text that exists in cell A1. The text is 9/12/2023, and it is centered across the selection, which is why it looks like it is in F15 on the screen. If you click on any of the objects, it will automatically take you to that location within the workbook.

​

If you were not aware of this feature, I hope you will use it to help you better navigate your workbooks.

Today's Playbook - A deep dive for the modern finance leader

​

Learning the ACE storytelling method

One of the most important skills for Finance professionals is becoming a competent and confident storyteller. This takes intentional practice and is often a neglected skill for Finance professionals. We often gravitate towards the latest technical training like power query, power pivot or Chat GPT. Technical skills continue to be very important and if they are complimented with strong communication and storytelling skills, it becomes a winning combination.

​

Warren Buffett famously said that his best career move was to take a public speaking course at the Dale Carnegie institute. The Dale Carnegie institute also published a study that said that 85% of our success as business professionals is driven by our soft (communication) skills.

​

The ACE framework is a one way to help hit the mark with storytelling.

​

​

A - Audience - always start with your audience and cater your message, email, or presentation to that audience. We often look at it from our perspective which often leads to a less than optimal result.

​

C - Content - Create insightful and interesting content. This should help your business stakeholder quickly understand the information and then move to discussion and decision making. Intentional visualization of data is often a great approach.

​

E - Execution - your body language and voice are tools that you can develop. This step is absolutely critical and is often missed. Turn your camera on and bring your authentic energy.

​

Lastly, being able to communicate confidently takes practice. The more time you invest in storytelling, the better you will become.

The FP&A Guy's Tech Tips

​

In the last newsletter, we listed Finance people to follow to stay up-to-date and learn more about Generative AI. Today I want to list some of the most popular Large Language Models available that you can experiment with. Below is a brief summary of a few popular models. For details on what LLMs are and how they are used in Generative AI, check out the article below from Computerworld.

​

​What are LLMs, and how are they used in generative AI? | Computerworld​

​

  • ​ChatGPT - This is the one that started all the discussion about LLMs and is the tool most people are familiar with. They have a free version of ChatGPT 3.5 that anyone can use and a paid version of ChatGPT 4.0. The paid version includes a code interpreter that allows you to upload files for use with the model. It also pulls data from the internet to help answer questions. ChatGPT was developed by OpenAI and is integrated in the new Microsoft CoPilot

​

  • ​Bard - Bard was developed by Google. The model is capable of integrating real-world data with Google Search. In my experience, I have found Bard to be less useful than ChatGPT, and it lacks a code interpreter. Google recently released Gemini, which is an Advanced AI Model.

​

  • ​Claude - Claude was developed by a startup called Anthropic, and it is backed by Amazon. The Claude language model is very good at processing information and is great for summarizing transcripts.

​

  • LlaMA - LlaMA was developed by Meta and is a large open-source LLM. This one requires installation to use, and I have not used it at this time and am not familiar with what would be the best use cases for it.

​

Ron's Recommendations

​

How passion in your work and life can turn the ordinary into the extraordinary.

​

The Fred Factor by Mark Sanborn is an inspiring short parable based on a real-life mail carrier who took his job to the next level.

​

Fred had exceptional customer service and treated every resident like they were his most important. For example, he offered to bundle Mark Sanborn's mail while he was on his speaking trips and put it around the side of the house so burglars would not be attracted to Mark's home.

​

Here are four important lessons from the book:

​

1) Everyone makes a difference - whether you are a Finance co-op student or the CFO, everyone can make a meaningful or exceptional difference if they CHOOSE to.

  • There are no unimportant jobs, just people who feel unimportant doing their jobs.

2) Success is built on relationships - invest in relationships by being genuinely curious and listening actively. We have to invest in relationships!

​

3) You must continually create value for others, and it doesn't have to cost a penny - this is where we can be creative and help solve our stakeholders' challenges.

​

4) You can reinvent yourself regularly. The famous quote 'life begins at the edge of your comfort zone comes to mind'.

​

I often look for Freds. People who make a meaningful difference in other people's lives.

​

It can be as simple as a smile or amazing service at a Coffee shop.

Imagine being a Fred as a Finance professional. This will lead much more fulfillment and success.
